topic: Choosing offset versus keyset pagination for REST APIs
tomorrowTopic: Diagnosing duplicate POST effects after client retries

hook.headline: Pagination is a consistency trade-off
hook.hook: OFFSET is simple and page-oriented; keyset pagination trades random page jumps for efficient, stable traversal by sort key.
hook.visualCaption: Offset locates rows by position; keyset locates the next page relative to the last sort key.
hook.microExample: page 500 → skip rows | cursor → continue after key

mentalModel.title: Position versus continuation key
mentalModel.coreIdea: Offset pagination asks the database to skip a position in an ordered result. Keyset pagination carries the last row's unique ordering values forward and filters relative to them, avoiding work proportional to a large offset when the query can use a suitable index.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Choose based on navigation needs, ordering guarantees, data churn, and the query plan—not API fashion.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: position → OFFSET | last key → seek → continue

code.title: Seek from the last row
code.intro: Use a deterministic ordering and carry every ordering column in the cursor predicate.
code.code:
SELECT id, created_at, total
FROM orders
WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2)
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 50;
code.highlightReason: The row comparison continues strictly after the previous page's final ordering tuple instead of skipping a numeric position.
code.takeaway: A tie-breaker such as id makes the ordering unique and prevents equal timestamps from creating an ambiguous boundary.
code.professionalNote: Cursor columns should have well-defined null handling, and the supporting index should match the filtering and ordering strategy.

production.title: Choose for the access pattern
production.scenario: An orders API serves both an admin screen that jumps to page numbers and an infinite-scroll activity feed with millions of rows and frequent inserts.
problems: Large offsets can require PostgreSQL to compute and discard many preceding rows before returning the requested page.
Concurrent inserts or deletes can shift positional pages, so separate offset requests may skip or repeat rows.
production.professionalApproach: Keep offset pagination where arbitrary page navigation matters and result sizes are controlled. Prefer keyset pagination for sequential feeds, with a unique deterministic order, opaque cursor, and an index validated using the actual query plan.
production.debugClue: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows high-offset requests processing many rows before a small LIMIT result is returned.

interview.question: When would you choose keyset pagination over LIMIT/OFFSET for a production REST endpoint?
interview.answer: I prefer keyset pagination for large, sequential result sets where users move forward or backward rather than jump to page 500. It continues from a deterministic sort key, so it avoids large OFFSET work and is less sensitive to positional shifts. OFFSET remains simpler when arbitrary page numbers are a real requirement. Neither approach gives snapshot consistency across separate requests by itself.
